text: The figure is radical: the Lord of the hour ({hour}) and the Lord of the Ascendant ({lord}) {why}. Lilly takes such a figure as "fit to be judged".
plain: The chart passes Lilly's first test (it is "radical"): {hour}, the planet of this hour, agrees with {lord}, the planet that stands for you (they {why}). Lilly would read this chart with confidence.
source: Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), "Considerations before Judgment", pp.121-123

text: The figure is not radical by Lilly's test: the Lord of the hour ({hour}) and the Lord of the Ascendant ({lord}) are neither the same planet, nor of one triplicity, nor of the same nature.
plain: The chart fails Lilly's first test: {hour}, the planet of this hour, and {lord}, the planet that stands for you, have nothing in common. Lilly would hesitate to read this chart at all, so hold everything else here lightly.
source: Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), "Considerations before Judgment", pp.121-123

text: Only {deg:.0f}° (rescaled) of {sign} rises. Lilly: when the first degrees of a sign ascend "you may not adventure judgment".
plain: The rising sign has only just begun to rise ({deg:.0f}° of its 30). Lilly thought it too early to judge: the situation is still forming.
source: Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), "Considerations before Judgment", pp.121-123
basis: sourced; degree rescaled to the IAU band (app)

text: {deg:.0f}° (rescaled) of {sign} rises. Lilly: when 27, 28 or 29 degrees ascend "it's no wayes safe to give judgment".
plain: The rising sign has almost finished rising ({deg:.0f}° of its 30). Lilly thought it unsafe to judge: the matter may already be settled, or about to change.
source: Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), "Considerations before Judgment", pp.121-123
basis: sourced; degree rescaled to the IAU band (app)

text: Ophiuchus is rising. It has no sign in Lilly, so the Ascendant has no Lord, and the radical test cannot be applied.
plain: Ophiuchus, the thirteenth constellation, is rising. Lilly's book has no sign for it, so no planet stands for you and his main tests cannot be applied. Lilly gives no rule for this case.
source: app rule

text: The Moon is in the Via Combusta ({where}). Lilly: it is "not safe to judge" then.
plain: The Moon is on the "burnt road" (Via Combusta), a stretch of the sky Lilly thought unlucky. He said it is not safe to judge then.
source: Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), "Considerations before Judgment", pp.121-123

text: The Moon is in the later degrees of {sign} ({deg:.0f}°, rescaled). Lilly warns against judging then, especially in Gemini, Scorpio or Capricorn.
plain: The Moon is at the very end of {sign}, about to change sign. Lilly warned against judging then: things are in transition.
source: Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), "Considerations before Judgment", pp.121-123

text: The Moon is void of course: she perfects no aspect before leaving {sign}. Lilly: "All manner of matters goe hardly on (except the principall significators be very strong) when the Moon is voyd of course"{soft}.
plain: The Moon is "void of course": she makes no further contact with any planet before she leaves her present constellation. Lilly says matters then go on with difficulty{soft_plain}: a better moment to finish, rest or plan than to start something new.
source: Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), "Considerations before Judgment", pp.121-123; definition p.112
basis: sourced; "before leaving the sign" uses the IAU band (app)

text: Saturn is in the Ascendant{retro}. Lilly, after the Arabians: "the matter of that Question seldome or never comes to good".
plain: Saturn, the planet of delay and patience, is rising{retro_plain}. Lilly, after older Arabic authors, was doubtful of matters begun now; read it as a call for patience and extra care.
source: Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), "Considerations before Judgment", pp.121-123

text: Saturn is in the seventh house. Lilly: this "either corrupts the judgement of the Astrologer, or is a Signe the matter propounded will come from one misfortune to another".
plain: Saturn, the planet of delay and patience, is in the 7th house, which stands for the other party and also for the astrologer. Lilly took this as a sign that the reading itself may go astray, so he would treat it with care.
source: Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), "Considerations before Judgment", pp.121-123

text: The Lord of the Ascendant ({lord}) is combust, {d:.1f}° from the Sun. Lilly: then "neither question propounded will take, or the Querent be regulated".
plain: {lord}, the planet that stands for you, is "combust": only {d:.1f}° from the Sun and lost in its glare. Lilly treats this as a serious weakness: you may feel overshadowed by circumstances, so it may be wiser to wait or to act with support.
source: Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), "Considerations before Judgment", pp.121-123

text: The Lord of the seventh ({lord7}) is {how}. Lilly: then "the Artist shall scarce give a solid judgment".
plain: {lord7}, the planet of the 7th house (other people, partners and the astrologer), is badly placed ({how}). Lilly says the reader can then hardly give a sound judgment.
source: Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), "Considerations before Judgment", pp.121-123

text: The Lord of the Ascendant's fortitudes and debilities are equal ({f} each). Lilly: "When the testimonies of fortunes and Infortunes are equal, deferre judgment".
plain: {lord}, the planet that stands for you, has exactly as many strengths as weaknesses ({f} each). Lilly's advice is to wait and judge later.
source: Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), "Considerations before Judgment", pp.121-123; scoring p.115, p.181
basis: sourced; applied to the Lord of the Ascendant (app)

text: The Lord of the Ascendant ({lord}) is strong: {f} fortitudes against {d} debilities (net {n:+d}), {cond}, in the {house} house.
plain: {lord}, the planet that stands for you, is strong ({f} points for, {d} against, net {n:+d}). In plain terms, you would be acting from a position of strength.
source: Lilly pp.115, 181 (subtract the lesser number from the greater)
basis: sourced method; the +5 threshold is an app rule

text: The Lord of the Ascendant ({lord}) is weak: {f} fortitudes against {d} debilities (net {n:+d}), {cond}, in the {house} house.
plain: {lord}, the planet that stands for you, is weak ({f} points for, {d} against, net {n:+d}). In plain terms, you may have less control over events than you would like; preparation and patience help.
source: Lilly pp.115, 181
basis: sourced method; the -5 threshold is an app rule

text: The Lord of the Ascendant is angular (house {house}). Lilly gives angles the greatest accidental strength (p.115).
plain: The planet that stands for you is in one of the four "angles" (house {house}), the most powerful places in the chart. It is well placed to act.
source: Lilly p.115

text: The Lord of the Ascendant is cadent (house {house}). Lilly gives cadent houses the least strength, and the twelfth a debility (p.115).
plain: The planet that stands for you is in a weak, "falling" house (house {house}). It has less room to act just now.
source: Lilly p.115

text: The Moon applies by {aspect} to {planet} ({dev:.1f}° from exact). In Lilly's judgments an application of the Moon to a fortune by sextile or trine promises the matter well.
plain: The Moon is moving towards a friendly contact ({aspect}) with {planet}, one of the two helpful planets (the fortunes"). Lilly reads this as a good sign for whatever is in hand."
source: Lilly Book II ch. XXI (perfection by aspect)

text: The Moon applies by {aspect} to {planet} ({dev:.1f}° from exact). In Lilly's judgments a square or opposition of an infortune hinders the matter.
plain: The Moon is moving towards a hard contact ({aspect}) with {planet}, one of the two difficult planets. Lilly reads this as an obstacle to work around.
source: Lilly Book II ch. XXI; p.106 (square = imperfect enmity, opposition = perfect hatred)

text: {planet} is in Cazimi, "in the heart of the Sun" (within 17'). All authors, Lilly says, hold such a planet "fortified thereby".
plain: {planet} is "cazimi", exactly in the heart of the Sun. Being near the Sun usually weakens a planet, but at the very centre it makes it very strong.
source: Lilly p.113

text: {a} and {b} are in mutual reception by {kind}. Lilly: "the strongest and best of all receptions" when by house; "the thing is brought to passe" when the significators receive each other.
plain: {a} and {b} each stand in the other's home ground ("mutual reception", by {kind}). Lilly thought this one of the surest signs that two parties work together and the thing comes about.
source: Lilly p.112

text: The Part of Fortune is angular (house {house}). Lilly: well posited or in an angle, "we judge the estate of the querent to be sound and firme".
plain: The Part of Fortune, a point standing for wealth and well-being, is in a strong place (house {house}). Lilly read this as a sound, secure position.
source: Lilly p.143

text: The Part of Fortune is cadent (house {house}). Lilly: if otherwise placed, "we doe the contrary".
plain: The Part of Fortune, a point standing for wealth and well-being, is in a weak place (house {house}). Lilly read this the other way: a less secure position.
source: Lilly p.143

text: {planet} is in Ophiuchus. That band has no sign in Lilly, so it is scored peregrine.
plain: {planet} is in Ophiuchus, which has no sign in Lilly, so the app gives it no rulership points. That counts against it.
source: app rule

text: There is no sunrise or sunset at this place today (polar day or night). The planetary hour uses equal hours from local mean midnight.
plain: There is no sunrise or sunset here today, so the planetary hours are approximated with equal hours.
source: app rule
